candidate.answerReason: A batch of 15 oranges costs 50 cents and sells for 60 cents, earning 10 cents. Ten batches earn 100 cents and contain 150 oranges.

methods.label: Find the profit on a common batch
methods.explanation:
Use a batch of \(15\) oranges so that both groups of \(3\) and groups of \(5\) divide evenly. Buying \(15\) oranges costs
\[
\frac{15}{3}\cdot10=50\text{ cents},
\]
while selling them brings in
\[
\frac{15}{5}\cdot20=60\text{ cents}.
\]
Thus each batch earns \(60-50=10\) cents. A profit of \(\$1.00=100\) cents requires \(100/10=10\) batches, containing \(10\cdot15=150\) oranges, choice B.
methods.levelReason: Common batches keep the reasoning entirely in whole-number price and profit arithmetic.
